summary: Batakrishna Ghosh (1905–1950) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who completed his doctoral studies under Hanns Oertel around 1932–1935. He served as a librarian at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and edited the Bulletin of Tibetology.

Beata Grant (born 1954) works in sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. After earning her Ph.D. from Stanford University, she was a postdoctoral fellow at UC Berkeley and became Associate Professor of Chinese Language and Literature at Washington University in St. Louis around 1992.

Beatrice Erskine Lane (1878–1939) was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied at Radcliffe College under William James, Josiah Royce, George Santayana, and George Herbert Palmer, and later at Columbia University. She was appointed professor at Otani University in 1921.

Beatrix Pfleiderer (1941–2011) was an Indologist who earned her degrees at the University of Heidelberg. She held posts at the University of Maryland, College Park, Heidelberg, Hamburg, European University Viadrina, and was a visiting professor at the University of Hawaiʻi.

Bedřich Hrozný (1879–1952) was a linguist, historian, and archaeologist who studied at the University of Vienna and the University of Berlin. He held academic posts at the University of Vienna (~1905–1919) and the University of Prague (~1919–1952).
Beiho Takashima (1875–1949) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar who studied at Toyo University and later held an academic post there. He also founded the Bukkyo Seito Doshikai.
Bemé Shyi Drol studied under Shechen Gyaltsab and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.

Ben Jiao is a Tibetologist who earned his Ph.D. at Case Western Reserve University under Melvyn C. Goldstein. As attested in 2008, he served as Deputy Director of the Contemporary Tibetan Research Institute at the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences.
Ben Joffe is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Colorado under the supervision of Carole McGranahan.

Benedetta Lomi, a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, received her PhD from SOAS University of London. She held posts at UC Berkeley, the University of Virginia (~2015–2017), and the University of Bristol (~2017).

Benimadhab Barua (1888–1948) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the University of Calcutta and the University of London. He was headmaster at Mahamuni Anglo-Pali Institution and taught at the University of Calcutta from 1913, serving as professor from 1918 to 1948.

Benjamin A. Elman (born 1946) is a sinologist and historian. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Pennsylvania under Nathan Sivin and Susan Naquin, later holding major professorial posts at UCLA (1986–2002) and Princeton University, where he directed the East Asian Studies Program in 2002.
Benjamin Bogin is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan, where he studied under Donald S. Lopez, Jr., Janet Gyatso, and Gareth Sparham.

Benjamin Brose is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who earned his Ph.D. at Stanford University under Carl Bielefeldt and Bernard Faure. Around 2010–2016, he served as assistant professor of Chinese Buddhism at the University of Michigan.
Benjamin Fleming is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who earned his PhD from McMaster University. He was affiliated with the City University of New York as attested in 2021.

Benjamin Lewis Rice (1837–1927) was an Indologist and archaeologist. He served as Director of Public Instruction in Mysore (~1868–1883), Secretary to the Education Commission of India (~1882–1883), and Director of the Mysore Archaeological Department (~1884–1889).

Benjamin W. Fortson IV is a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He completed studies at Yale University (~1989–1993) and Harvard University (~1993–1996), and held a post at the University of Michigan around 2003.

Benjamin Wood is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who earned his Doctor of Philosophy from the University of Toronto under doctoral supervisor Frances Garrett, while also studying under Khenpo Kunga Sherab, Shayne Clarke, and Thubten Champa.

Benkyo Shiio (1876–1971) was a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate from the University of Tokyo. He taught at Shukyo, Nihon, and Waseda Universities, served as president of Taisho University (1926) and Tokai Gakuen Women's College (1963), and headed the Sanko Library.

Benoytosh Bhattacharyya (1897–1964) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the Universities of Calcutta and Dhaka under teachers Haraprasad Shastri and Alfred Foucher. He served as General Editor of Gaekwad's Oriental Series and Director of the Oriental Institute, Vadodara.
